hook_text: You've LIVED a business cycle. Nobody gave you the names.
clip_script: Think of a year you remember when things were good: the rank buzzing, shops hiring, everyone's cousin finding work. And a year when things were tight: quiet tills, short shifts, 'we're not taking anyone now.' Same town. Same people. Different years. That difference, repeating, is the business cycle — the economy breathing in and out. Breathing in: more work makes more spending makes more work. Full lungs — the peak: everything flat out, prices creeping. Breathing out: orders slow, retrenchments start, each cut spends less at the next shop. Empty — the trough: the hardest stretch... where recovery quietly gathers: things cheap, borrowing easier, worn things needing replacement. And how do you see the turn coming? Headlights: building plans, new orders — decisions about tomorrow, they bend first. Speedometer: this month's sales. Rearview mirror: unemployment — it peaks AFTER the worst is over. The economy breathes. Now you can hear it.
visual_style: A township high street cycling through boom and quiet in timelapse, breathing with a visible rhythm; then a taxi dashboard overlay — headlights, speedometer, mirror — each lighting up with its indicator.
pacing: Breathing tempo — swelling and easing with the phases, snapping crisp for the dashboard.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read the country's breathing like an economist.
